result.title: EVD-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for EEG-to-Image Decoding
result.summary: EEG-to-image decoding recovers visual information from non-invasive brain recordings, providing a window into human perception. However, comparisons across systems are confounded by a variable that is rarely reported as such: which participants' data the system was allowed to use. The same Top-1 score on a 200-way gallery may come from a per-participant system, a pooled model over all participants, or a model that never saw the test participant---cases that differ by more than most architectural changes between the methods being compared. We present \bench, a benchmark on THINGS-EEG2 that standardizes the gallery and EEG input, matches training budgets across systems within each regime, and compares three participant-access regimes: within-subject, joint-subject, and strict leave-one-subject-out, with unlabeled target calibration reported separately. All three settings evaluate concept-level zero-shot retrieval: the 200 test concepts are disjoint from the 1,654 concepts used for EEG--image fitting and validation. We compare retrieval across access regimes and use zero-EEG and matched-wrong EEG controls to assess dependence on correct EEG--stimulus pairing. We vary trial averaging, gallery size and difficulty, and training data coverage, and compare target adaptation and visual feature targets. We also assess sensitivity to EEG window length and channel count, robustness to input perturbations, and confidence calibration. These results establish participant-access regime as a necessary reporting dimension alongside gallery, repetition, and visual target.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 EVD-Bench，在 THINGS-EEG2 上统一 gallery 与 EEG 输入、匹配训练预算，系统比较 within-subject、joint-subject 与严格留一被试三种被试访问设定下的概念级零样本检索，并做 trial 平均、gallery 规模、EEG 时长与通道、置信校准等消融。
AI.relevance_reason: 属脑信号解码这一较远领域，但其「零 EEG 与错配 EEG」对照用于检验结果是否真正依赖正确刺激配对，可能为 LVR 中 latent 内容是否被答案实际使用的因果核查与报告规范提供借鉴，宜作背景性阅读。
